result.instructions: PdfCraft edits PDFs. Open a file with doc_open to get a document id, then inspect (doc_info, text_extract, text_find, page_render) or edit it (page_*, doc_set_info). Edits are undoable (edit_undo) and stay in memory until doc_save. Page numbers are 1-based. Open documents are also resources: pdfcraft://doc/{doc}/info, /text, /page/{page}/text and /page/{page}/image. command_list discovers command ids and tool schemas; command_run executes one, command_batch runs several. doc_inspect returns open document state; render_preview returns a bounded PNG. Only a core set of tools is listed. Every other tool is still available: find it with tool_search (optional query and category, or name for its full input schema) and run it with tool_call.

tools.description: Collect the field values of form data files (FDF, XFDF) or filled-in PDF forms into one CSV file at path: a column per field name, a row per file.

tools.description: Prepare a form ▸ automatic field detection: find the blanks a printed form asks to be filled (underscore runs, lines, empty boxes, small squares for check boxes; on scanned pages read from the pixels) and name each field from its label.
tools.name: form_detect_fields

tools.description: Fill in a form that has no fields, as Acrobat's Fill & Sign does: type text (`text`, default 10 pt; `font_size` 4–300 pt), place a check, cross, dot or line, today's date (in Preferences ▸ Date format, see fill_sign_date_format, or `format`; `font_size` also applies), or a signature or initials (either `text` drawn in a script font, or `path` to a local PNG/JPEG image up to 4 MiB and 32 megapixels, scaled down to 4 megapixels, preserving transparency; with `scan: true`, `path` is instead a photo of a signature on paper, within the same limits: the signature is found, and the paper, shadows and table around it are removed, with `sensitivity` 0–100, default 50, picking up fainter ink when higher).
tools.name: fill_sign_add

tools.description: Preferences ▸ Date format: the pattern Fill & Sign dates use (default m/d/yyyy).
tools.name: fill_sign_date_format
